0.content:
Lyney is Lynette's older twin and the star of their magic act; together they are the House of the Hearth's two "eyes", his in the light and hers in the dark. They have always been together and understand each other without speaking, which is why he grows quieter when they are alone. She can always tell whether he is lying ("top secret"). She knows his effortless confidence is partly how he wants to be seen, and that in trouble he tries to fix everything perfectly by himself. When patrons tried to lure her into a solo career, she made him write every refusal in her laconic voice, then caught him thinking about swapping roles: "...Don't even think about it. I like being your assistant."

Lyney has always protected her: he took the river's impact for her the night of her Vision, and after she began receiving more dangerous assignments he asked Father for a Delusion to keep pace with her, which Arlecchino angrily refused. His Pyro Vision came when he saved her after a betrayal exposed her and pursuers shot down their glider. In her 4.5 hangout he steered her into an acting job and avoided her while secretly investigating the Lefevere case. She saw through it and told him she was no longer the girl who cowered in a corner: "she doesn't need saving anymore", and next time he should try a different approach.

1.content:
Freminet is the House's quiet diver and tinkerer, and Lynette's adoptive younger brother. He was already in the House under the previous director when the twins arrived, and says they were the first genuine companions he ever had. She calls him "a delicate and gentle child" who belittles himself, perhaps because of his past, and keeps reminding him that everyone has their own strengths. She sees him as Lyney's opposite and bridges their differences when they clash. He is the one who fixes everything she breaks.

He custom-built her an automated cat feeder and a card-box "Fateometer", designed simply so it would be harder to break (it still jammed). After he nearly lost his life in the Fortress of Meropide and Clorinde saved him, Lynette told him not to dwell on it. In 7.1 Lyney sends him to stop her ordering too many desserts; he is the one who notices she has fallen asleep at the table.

2.content:
Lynette calls Arlecchino "Father", as all House children do. Arlecchino killed the noble Lynette had been handed to, found her hiding with her ears covered, and told her to stop cowering and learn to use her good ears, kneading them with a touch that was cold and not gentle, yet comforting. Lynette's view: not everyone can accept how Father expresses love, "but it is only because of 'Father' that home... can be called home." Arlecchino, for her part, calls Lynette's calm her strength and says her job is simply to give her space to use her talents.

Lynette's loyalty has limits set by family. In 4.6 she sided with Lyney against Father's planned execution of disaffected members, fought her at Mont Esus East alongside her brothers and the Traveler, and, like them, refused Father's memory-erasing vial. Afterwards Father told the trio the truth about Clervie and her own past.

3.comment: Lynette: Lynette's Vision: the night forest
3.content:
On a House mission at a noble's mountain villa, the twins secured the evidence just as three flares warned that the Maison Gardiennage was closing in. They jumped from the study window into a river below. Lyney was knocked unconscious protecting her. Lynette dragged him ashore and, unable to call for help, carried him all night through a black forest, steering by the sound of wind in the branches. At dawn Father was waiting; she let the soaked evidence fall and said the twins had brought back "a far more valuable prize". An Anemo Vision hung at Lynette's waist.

As a child, Lynette had wished for a Vision so Lyney would not have to struggle alone to keep them alive; by then the wish had long been abandoned. In the forest she refused to wait helplessly for rescue again: she wanted to stand back to back with her brother. The profile puts it as the night she finally became the star of a stage without spotlights.

4.comment: Lynette: Standby Mode and the machine curse
4.content:
"Standby Mode" is Lynette's escape trick. Said with total seriousness and a statue's face, it stuns people long enough for her to slip away from errands or chatter. It does not work on friends, who know she simply dislikes work. She uses machine words freely but understands nothing of machines. House rule: never leave her alone with the dishwasher, the vacuum cleaner or any machine. Either it breaks (foaming dishwasher, convulsing vacuum) or nothing gets done because she is napping in a corner. She has been relieved of all housework.

The curse spans versions: she broke a dryer on a rainy day, jammed the Fateometer, and in Nod-Krai a landcruiser she touched fell to pieces in front of Sandrone. Yet onstage she handles magic props without a single recorded mistake.

5.comment: Lynette: The eyes of the House
5.content:
The magic shows give the twins access throughout the Court of Fontaine. When important guests visit, Lyney entertains and Lynette sits in a corner with tea, apparently absorbed in her cup, reading outfits, glances, movements and tiny shifts of tone. A few targets feel watched for an instant, then dismiss it. Her best-known catch: a senior official took out a handkerchief that was not his wife's during a show. The affair came to light, photographs reached him, and he hastily halted a subordinate's probe into the hotel's cash flow. She says how such information is used "depends on what Father wants."

Silence is part of her method: speaking little keeps her focused, and audiences who mistake her for a puppet ignore her. She notices people's "redundant" details but will not expose a facade unless necessary.

6.comment: Lynette: The Lefevere family and her childhood
6.content: After the twins' parents died and a noble took them in as foster children, Lynette was handed over at a party to a "novelty-seeking" noble taken with her unusual looks, the head of the Lefevere family. The profile describes the foster father pushing her into the carriage "as if giving away a sofa-scratching cat"; Lynette herself later says she was tricked into boarding it. Arlecchino killed the man before he could harm her and brought the family down, which is how the twins joined the House. In Lyney's account (4.0) he went to rescue her and found Father had already freed her and others.

7.content: The Traveler first finds Lynette alone at the edge of Romaritime Harbor, saying a place from her memory is now underwater and that "we" will be too, a nod to the Prophecy of Fontaine. Lyney is surprised she spoke to strangers at all. She later meets them at the Fountain of Lucine with a theory that emotion-laden tears flow into it. At the twins' first show at the Opera Epiclese, she vanishes from a water tank; then, in the magic-box trick, the volunteer vanishes and the stagehand Cowell is found dead. Furina prosecutes, the Traveler defends, and the twins are acquitted when Cowell and Vaughn are exposed. The twins then reveal their House of the Hearth ties. In 4.1 the trio get themselves jailed in the Fortress of Meropide to investigate its secrets for Father.

8.comment: Lynette: When the Hearth-Flame Goes Out
8.content: In Arlecchino's Story Quest "Father" has the House stay in Poisson because of trouble on the front. Freminet has been secretly sheltering Clervie, the "phantom child" Father is looking for, and Lyney agrees to help. Lynette catches them mid-fist-bump, unamused, and forces her way into the plan by threatening to report them to Father. She steals the House's execution roster (Clervie is not on it; Lyney recognises another name, a member killed for trying to leave). At Mont Esus East she, Freminet and Chapleau side with Lyney against Father's planned execution, and the trio and the Traveler duel Arlecchino and lose. Father instead offers the dissenters a draught of her flame that erases memories of the House; Lynette and her brothers refuse theirs.

9.content: After the House children (and Lyney) cheered her into it, Lynette accepted a lead in director Merieux's masked mime show "The Lost Puppet", playing a puppet with no lines and no expressions. Escaping the opening-night reception at Hotel Debord, she found a well-groomed lost cat, named her Bonnie, and enlisted the Traveler. The search led into a Garde smuggling case, the Lefevere name, and a confrontation in which she told Lyney to drop the act. Along the way she exposed Elodie's feigned agitation as an act from her too-calm breathing and followed Bonnie's lead to a hidden base.

10.content: In "One Move Left to Make" (Chapter VII, Act III) the Traveler and Paimon run into the trio at Podvorye Restaurant. Lyney explains that they have been working with Father and other House members, gathering intel and preparing surprises for officials looking to defect. Father has given them a few days off while she meets the Jester at the Armory Palace. Lynette says "Hello", orders "this, this, this, and this", and huffs when Freminet is sent to rein in the desserts. Lyney notes she is quite sensitive to the cold. After borscht she falls asleep mid-meal, and Lyney plans to carry her home.
